title: fix(driver-sql): update() stamps updated_at into a fresh object, never the caller's data
body:
Fixes #24835

Clause-②: no

Round 2 of the card, option A of the fork in report `6289852046`: the producer fix. Round 1 was PR #24862, the log level of a lost delivery. It landed on `main` as `3fbef41b4a`, and this PR does not touch its file. Cross-lane: `driver-sql` is `domain:engine`'s code, declared on #6367 (comment `6289887999`).

## What was wrong

`SqlDriver.update()` assigned its `updated_at` stamp onto `formatted`. `formatInput` and `applyWriteColumnMap` are copy-on-write: a patch that needs no coercion comes back as the caller's own object. So the stamp landed in the caller's `data`. ObjectQL passes `hookContext.input.data` to `driver.update` and then publishes that same object as `DataEvent.changes`.

On PostgreSQL and MySQL the stamp is `knex.fn.now()`, a knex `Raw` holding the client, its pool and a Node `Timeout`. The webhook outbox's `JSON.stringify(payload)` threw (`Converting circular structure to JSON`), so no `sys_http_delivery` row was written for any record update. The record write still answered 200, and the webhook still read active. On SQLite the stamp is an ISO string: it serialises, and it is just as foreign to the caller's patch. `rotatedUpdateById()` had the same in-place stamp. `updateMany()` already built a fresh object.

## What this PR changes

`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts`, two sites, both now in `updateMany`'s shape. Line numbers are at base `950f949a9c`.

- `update()` (`:8820`): `const stamped = { ...formatted, updated_at: this.updatedAtStamp() }`, passed to both the presumed-timestamp path and the plain path. `updateWithPresumedTimestamp`'s fallback already builds its own unstamped copy.
- `rotatedUpdateById()` (`:10249`): `payload` is the stamped copy, or `formatted` when nothing is stamped.
- `stampUpsertUpdatedAt` (`:8554`) is **unchanged, measured**. Its only caller is `upsert()` (`:9580`), and there `formatted` is derived from `toUpsert = { ...rest }` (`:9482`), a fresh object built from `const { _id, ...rest } = data` (`:9481`). The stamp can land only in the driver's own copy, never in the caller's object. `grep stampUpsertUpdatedAt packages/drivers/*/src` finds no other caller.
- Not touched: `applyTenantScope`, any other driver method, objectql (option B, not taken), `packages/spec`, round 1's file.

## Pins

1. `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-24835-update-leaves-caller-data.test.ts`, on SQLite. `update()` leaves its `data` argument `toStrictEqual` to a `structuredClone` taken before the call. It covers four cases:
   - the plain path (a table the driver's DDL created);
   - the presumed-timestamp path with the column present;
   - the presumed-timestamp path with the column absent (the fallback that drops the stamp);
   - the rotated path.

   Each case also proves the stamp really ran on that path: the stored `updated_at` moved off a backdated value, the presumption settled, or the column read as `absent`.
2. `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-delivery-real-sql-driver.test.ts` runs a real `ObjectQL` and a real `SqlDriver` (SQLite) with an active declared webhook, through the production wiring: `AutoEnqueuer`, then `MessagingService.enqueueHttp`, then `SqlHttpOutbox`. An insert and a by-id update store 2 `sys_http_delivery` rows (`ref_id` `declared:probe_task_changed`). Each row's `payload_json` parses to plain JSON and re-serialises byte-identical, and nothing was logged as lost.
   - To support it, `plugin-webhooks` gains `@objectstack/driver-sql` as a devDependency (`pnpm-lock.yaml`: the importer entry only, 3 lines; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes).
   - Its `vitest.config.ts` aliases `@objectstack/driver-sql` to source, as it already does for `core` and `types`. The verdict is about the checkout, not `dist/`.
   - No PostgreSQL in a committed test: the live-PG/MySQL driver lane (`Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`) does not run on pull requests.

## Measured on a throwaway local PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster

I ran pin 2's own body against PG through a generated, uncommitted copy that changes only the driver config:

| tree | `sys_http_delivery` rows | update row |
|---|---|---|
| the in-place stamp put back (ablation leg A below) | **1** (`data.record.created` only) | missing; the pin fails on the label set |
| this branch `5755b9d424` | **2** (`data.record.created`, `data.record.updated`) | `payload_json` `changes` = `{"title": "webhook probe"}`, exactly the caller's patch |

Round 1 measured the same 1 row at base `41646a5788`, with the card's WARN. The cluster was stopped and deleted afterwards.

## Ablation (one leg per changed site)

Both legs used `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. Each restore was `git checkout HEAD`, proven by the blob `ecc2686b44a1` equal to the HEAD blob and an empty `git diff HEAD`, both re-checked by hand.

- **Leg A, `update()`.** `const stamped = { ...formatted, … }` was replaced with `formatted.updated_at = this.updatedAtStamp(); const stamped = formatted;`. Anchor 1 to 0; blob `ecc2686b44a1` to `cfad3f1e1a3b`.
  - Pin 1: `Tests 3 failed | 1 passed (4)`. The plain and both presumed cases are red. The rotated case stays green, because it goes through the other site.
  - Pin 2 on SQLite: `1 passed`. That is expected: an ISO string serialises, which is why SQLite never showed the loss.
  - Pin 2 on PG: `1 failed`, `expected [ 'data.record.created' ] to deeply equal [ 'data.record.created', …(1) ]`.
- **Leg B, `rotatedUpdateById()`.** The stamped copy was replaced with `Object.assign(formatted, { updated_at: … })`. Anchor 1 to 0; blob `ecc2686b44a1` to `d6664cc75a61`.
  - Pin 1: `Tests 1 failed | 3 passed (4)`. Only the rotated case is red.

Both subjects are imported from source (pin 1 relative, pin 2 through the alias), so no `dist/` leg was needed.

## Tests

All runs below are on the final head `7c88888b50` and under `os-verify-lock`, unless a line names another head.

- `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/plugin-webhooks^...' --filter='@objectstack/driver-sql...'`: `BUILD_EXIT=0`, `Tasks: 16 successful, 16 total`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: `Test Files 225 passed | 11 skipped (236)`, `Tests 3691 passed | 208 skipped (3899)`. The skips are this package's live-PG/MySQL cells, which are not provisioned locally.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql typecheck`: exit 0. The tsconfig `include` is `src/**/*`, so the new pin is compiled.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-webhooks exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: `Test Files 22 passed (22)`, `Tests 227 passed (227)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-webhooks typecheck`: exit 0 (`check:test-typecheck: OK`).
- The two pins alone, on `5755b9d424`: pin 1 `Tests 4 passed (4)`, pin 2 `Tests 1 passed (1)`. The ablation legs and the PG runs above are on `5755b9d424` too. The only later change to these files is `05079c544e`, which removed two `as any` option casts from pin 2 (the query-options-erasure ratchet counts them).

## Gates

The local subset was derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at the final head `7c88888b50`: 87 families over the 7 changed paths. One runner ran them, each under its own `os-verify-lock` acquisition, with every exit captured before any pipe.

- **84 families exited 0.** Among them: `check:undeclared-dep-imports` (the new devDependency), `check:test-source-alias` (the new alias), `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:driver-conformance`, `check:durability-log-level`, `check:turbo-task-graph`, `check:workspace-manifest-cycles`, `check:override-consistency`, `check:published-files`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-empty-changeset`.
- **2 families are NOT MEASURED: exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET.** `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` needs every package's `dist/`. `check:i18n` needs the CLI build closure. CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` runs both.
- **1 family is a declared narrowing, not run locally.** `check:type-check-debt` (`--re-measure`) rebuilds the whole monorepo under the shared lock from inside its own gate. CI runs it.

`--ran` reconciliation: `87 derived, 84 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED, 1 UNRUN` (the UNRUN is the declared `check:type-check-debt`).

An earlier run of the same battery, at `5755b9d424`, found one real red: `check:query-options-erasure`, `test surface grew 236 → 237`, from an `as any` on engine options in pin 2. `05079c544e` removed the casts, and the gate is green on the final head. CI check-runs were not concluded when this body was written; the report on #24835 cites them.

## Acceptance notes

- Before opening this PR I merged `origin/main` `7035682c8d` (merge commit `7c88888b50`). It brought round 1's landing (`3fbef41b4a`, the error-level report of a lost delivery) and a version-packages commit, both into `plugin-webhooks`. The merge was clean, and the branch's delta against main is still exactly the 7 files above.
- Every other reader of the update event's `changes`, and of `hookContext.input.data` after the driver call, now sees the caller's patch rather than a dialect value object. Examples: `afterUpdate` hooks and realtime subscribers. Only the webhook reader is pinned here.
